code: export function quickSort(a: readonly number[]): number[] { const arr = [...a]; const part = (lo, hi) => { if (lo >= hi) return; let i = lo; for (let j = lo; j < hi; j++) { if (arr[j] < arr[hi]) { [arr[i], arr[j]] = [arr[j], arr[i]]; i++; } } [arr[i], arr[hi]] = [arr[hi], arr[i]]; part(lo, i - 1); part(i + 1, hi); }; part(0, arr.length - 1); return arr; }
name: quickSort
summary: Quick sort - Lomuto partition around the last element, recursing each side. Harvested from base-studio-code's algorithm-visualization gallery (viz/examples/sorts.ts): the partitioning IS the animation - the pivot mark and the swap-into-place are the real algorithm's own steps.

vizCode: ({ datatype: 'array', input: [5, 2, 9, 1, 6, 3, 8, 4, 7], run(a) { const part = (lo, hi) => { if (lo >= hi) return; a.mark(hi, 'pivot'); let i = lo; for (let j = lo; j < hi; j++) { a.cursor('j', j); if (a.compare(j, hi) < 0) { a.swap(i, j); i++; } } a.swap(i, hi); part(lo, i - 1); part(i + 1, hi); }; part(0, a.length - 1); a.markSorted(); } })
